ingredients.item: pork shoulder or collar , sliced 4 mm against the grain
gochugaru — the ceiling dial; 1 tbsp for a mild table
/2 Asian pear , grated and squeezed nearly dry
scallions , sliced; 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds
Steamed rice , lettuce ssam, ssamjang , kimchi , thick garlic coins, and cold oi muchim — heat on the plate wants cold crunch beside it

instructions.heading: Fire hot, batches small
instructions.action: Fire hot, batches small. Charcoal or cast-iron at a solid medium-high — a pan surface around 200 °C, oil just at the shimmer. The slices go on in one loose layer — piled pork steams in the paste's moisture, and steamed paste is bitter. Single layer, sixty to ninety seconds undisturbed.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: the paste should sizzle and darken one shade, and the air should carry toasted chile and sesame. Black edges in the first minute mean the fire is a notch past the paste's tolerance — raise the grate or bank the coals and continue.

instructions.heading: Flip at the weep, pull fast
instructions.action: Flip at the weep, pull fast. Turn the slices when the edges bead juice and the underside is brick-brown, 60–90 seconds more on the second side, off the fire while the centers still carry a blush of juice. Pork shoulder at 4 mm is done in under three minutes a batch; every extra ten seconds trades juice for toughness.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: test piece at the grill station: glazed edge, juicy-fatty interior, heat arriving after the sweet on the finish. If the center is dry, the batch was thin-spread and overcooked — next batch spends less time on the second side.

instructions.heading: The two ways to eat it, both correct
instructions.action: The two ways to eat it, both correct. The ssam way: leaf, thin ssamjang swipe, a hot slice, garlic coin, fold, one bite — the record's full ceremony. The weeknight way: rice in a bowl, a stack of slices over, sesame and scallion, the pan's juice spooned last. Same meat, two speeds.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: the bowl test: the juice over rice should be red-gold and savory-sweet, milder than the slices taste plain — if it runs bitter, the pan's sugared drippings caught fire at some point and the heat was a notch high throughout; note it for next time, eat around it now.

visualDonenessCues: The slice: 4 mm against the grain, shoulder or collar, marinated 2–8 hours in a smooth paste.
The grill: single loose layer, flip at the beading edge, brick-brown not black, under three minutes a batch.
The pull: juicy centers with a blush of juice, never gray-through.
The table: ssam or rice-bowl, cold banchan in reach, heat dialed for the end of the meal.
storageNotes: Marinated pork keeps 24 hours (freeze flat up to a month). Cooked, 3 days — and the leftovers are arguably the record's second life: kimchi fried rice with diced dwaeji bulgogi, or a melt-grade cheese-and-dwaeji quesadilla that the fusion lane would claim if it could.

Variations: the same paste on pork belly slabs (#M11's slower cousin); on chicken thighs (#M17); thinned with mirin into a glaze for the shrimp record (#SF01). The soy-pork fork without heat is ganjang pork bulgogi (#M14).
